content: The assessment of glycemic status in individuals with diabetes is typically conducted using several methods, including the measurement of hemoglobin A1C, blood glucose monitoring (BGM) through finger-stick devices, and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems. Clinical trials have demonstrated that reducing A1C levels leads to improved glycemic control and better health outcomes for individuals with diabetes. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), in particular, provides detailed insights into blood glucose fluctuations, enabling individuals to manage their meals, physical activities, and medications more effectively. CGM has been shown to be especially advantageous for individuals undergoing insulin therapy, as it enhances self-management and supports better glycemic control in people with diabetes.
